title: Kneipp intervention for children in rehabilitation (KIKeR pilot) as a supplement to standard care for chronic respiratory diseases: feasibility and pilot study (WP2)
summary:
The aim of the project is to develop and test a treatment concept based on Kneipp therapy that is to be used as a supplement to the usual treatment of asthma in children. The focus is on water applications, which can help strengthen the immune system and promote children's health in the long term. Initial studies show that regular Kneipp applications can reduce the frequency of infections and sick days in children.
The study consists of two phases: In the first phase, it will be examined whether the Kneipp concept can be well integrated into daily treatment. For this purpose, experts as well as different groups will be interviewed. Subsequently, a pilot study will test how practicable and accepted the concept is among children aged 4 to 6 years who suffer from asthma and are undergoing rehabilitation.
In the long term, the project aims to scientifically validate naturopathic methods such as Kneipp applications and better integrate them into pediatric rehabilitation. The results of this study serve as the basis for larger clinical investigations and the further development of care for children with chronic respiratory diseases.

interventions.name:
The intervention is divided into two work packages and will be carried out over a period of 15 months (through December 2026). The first work package has already been approved (WP1, Ethics Committee Decision EA2_233_25 dated November 22, 2025, Registration No. DRKS00038097).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•    Clinically diagnosed bronchial asthma (ICD: J45)
•    Age 4–6 years
•    Regularly scheduled four-week inpatient rehabilitation stay
•    Written consent from the parents
Exclusion criteria:
•    Acute asthma exacerbation
•    Unstable asthma (e.g., recurrent dyspnea, increased need for rescue medication)
•    General condition with reduced exercise tolerance or clinical impairment
•    Severe chronic comorbidities with contraindications to thermal stimuli
•    Decompensated cardiorespiratory diseases
•    Allergic or bronchospastic reactions to medicinal plants or essential oils used
•    Lack of medical clearance due to medical uncertainty
